text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Pager: high error rate on hosted inference (us-west-2). Triggered SLO alert (5xx > 3% over 5m).

ashley: seeing 502/503s from model-service-canary. Dashboard shows memory on canary nodes spiking then OOMs. Topology: canary = 10% traffic to new batching runtime.

matt: paging and joining. Is this the new continuous-batching change?

samir: yep. New kernel selection + batching landed in canary cluster this morning. We pushed ~06:42 UTC.

jules: deploy-bot: rollout started 2025-11-15 06:42:03 UTC -> canary(10%) -> staged.

ashley: customer impact: increased 5xx for some low-latency routes (chat/generate). Token-level errors spiked, some sessions got partial outputs then errors.

oncall-sre: I’ve drained one canary node and repro'd locally: KV cache growth > expected, memory pressure triggers OOM killer on the runtime process.

matt: what does automated rollback status show?

deploy-bot: Automated rollback check: health_deviation > threshold. Auto-rollback initiated for canary at 06:48:12 UTC but one canary pod failed to terminate due to preStop hook hanging. Rollback incomplete (3/5 pods rolled back).

samir: preStop hook is a graceful flush of KV cache. Looks like the hook blocks on a background thread that's stuck in a kernel-roofline path introduced in this change.

lia: trying to flip feature flag kill-switch now: ff-toggle --env prod --flag batching-v2 --off

ashley: lia, do we rely on the flag for routing? The rollout used a runtime-level kernel change plus flag.

lia: flag API returned 200 but toggled state is still true in the control plane cache. UI shows OFF but the canary agents still read true. Possibly a stale config cache.

jules: that matches the logs: control-plane push succeeded, but agent debug shows last_update = 06:42 and no subsequent update.

matt: okay we have two failure modes: (A) automated rollback incomplete due to hanging preStop, (B) feature-flag kill-switch not picked up by agents due to stale config cache. Need manual mitigation to stop traffic to canary and evacuate in-flight requests.

oncall-sre: I can run iptables redirect to pin traffic away from canary pool. Suggest: route-remove canary-target-group from router, or set weight=0 for canary upstream.

samir: I can do the router weight change. Command: `rb-router set-weight --pool model-service-canary --weight 0`

lia: confirm: this will move 100% traffic back to stable?

samir: yes. Will do in 5s.

ashley: please add a note in chat when done and we’ll watch errors. Also plan for manual pod kill to finish rollback.

samir: rb-router set-weight ... done.

incident-bot: Traffic shift: canary weight -> 0% at 06:53:07 UTC.

matt: errors dropping?

ashley: dashboards show 5xx trending down within a minute, p50 latency slightly increased while stable handles burst.

jules: good. Now manual remediation for stuck pods: oncall-sre, can you escalate kill of preStop-hung processes? We should avoid hard node reboot if possible.

oncall-sre: I'll run `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` for the hung pods. Targeting pod model-canary-5 and model-canary-7.

lia: pausing the fancy shutdown to avoid KV corrupt: we will snapshot caches first. oncall-sre, do not hard kill until we dump state: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /app/tools/dump-kv.sh /tmp/kv.dump`

oncall-sre: OK dumping now.

matt: any customer-facing action needed? Should we open a notice?

ashley: short blip, <0.5% of active sessions had aborted outputs. I'll draft a brief status update: "We're investigating elevated errors; traffic moved off canary and service is stabilizing. More details to follow."

samir: dumps completed. Proceeding with forced delete on two pods.

oncall-sre: `kubectl delete --force --grace-period=0 pod/model-canary-5 pod/model-canary-7` done. New stable pods launching.

deploy-bot: Rollback verification: all canary pods terminated or replaced. Canary pool now empty.

lia: control plane cache fix: restarting config-agent on canary subscription cluster was needed. I restarted `config-agent` on control-plane mesh to ensure flag sync.

matt: can you confirm flag state on agents?

lia: agent debug: batching-v2 = OFF (seen by agents at 06:54:28 UTC).

ashley: monitoring: error rate back under SLO threshold. Latency back to baseline within 3m.

jules: good. Postmortem action items (quick): 1) fix preStop hook so it times out if flush stalls; 2) ensure feature flag push includes agent-level ack and backoff; 3) add probe to abort rollout earlier if KV growth > X.

samir: assigning myself to preStop hook fix. Will open PR and test in staging.

lia: I'll own agent ack requirement and implement forced refresh for flags after 10s.

matt: oncall-sre please file runbook entry for manual evacuation with `rb-router set-weight` and forced pod delete steps.

oncall-sre: filing runbook now, will add commands and caveats about dumping KV first.

ashley: draft incident page with timeline and impact and assign postmortem lead (samir). I'll ping customer success to prepare any outreach if they get questions.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Created incident ticket I-20251115-001.

matt: thanks all. Quick retro note: prefer gating KV growth as a canary metric so we fail fast before customer impact.

ashley: agreed. Closing thread after postmortem begins. :thumbsup:
